_readme: Profile research for PRO-99 Kleiner Perkins (COLLECTION.md s11), per scratch/PROFILE-BRIEF.md. Written 2026-09-30 by the profile-research agent. Form D facts from the bulk zips via build-firm-profile.own_fund_filings (scratchpad/profile/own-fund-filings.json); pre-2009 filings are paper REGDEX with no machine-readable amounts.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins XXII
funds.note: Firm post 2026-03-24: 'KP22, a $1 billion fund to back early-stage companies'. Form D 0002115014-26-000001 (2026Q2) TOTALAMOUNTSOLD $995,000,000 of $995,000,000 offered, first sale 2026-03-23; ADV 7.B.(1) GAV $995,000,000. Publish $995M with the accession (the firm rounds to $1B), or $1B firm-stated without it. KP XXII Friends, LLC (CIK 2114662) filed 0002114662-26-000001: $50M offered, $0 sold (side fund, not listed).

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Select Fund IV
funds.note: Firm post 2026-03-24: '$2.5 billion in growth funds'; Select IV is $1.92B of that on Form D 0002114651-26-000001 (TOTALAMOUNTSOLD $1,920,000,000, first sale 2026-03-23); ADV GAV $1,920,000,000. Select IV Friends (CIK 2114655) filed $100M offered, $0 sold.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Flex I
funds.note: Part of the '$2.5 billion in growth funds' (post URL slug ends 'select-iv-flex'; the text does not name Flex). Form D 0002114646-26-000001 TOTALAMOUNTSOLD $555,000,000, first sale 2026-03-23; ADV GAV $550,000,000. Select IV $1.92B + Flex I $555M = $2.475B, the firm's '$2.5 billion'.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins XXI
funds.note: Firm post 2024-06-28: 'KP21, an $825M fund to back early stage companies'. Form D TOTALAMOUNTSOLD $825,000,000, first sale 2024-06-28. KP XXI Friends (CIK 2027883): $50M offered, $0 sold.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Select Fund III
funds.note: Firm post 2024-06-28: 'KP Select III, a $1.2 billion fund to back high inflection investments'. Form D filed under accession prefix 0002027881 (XXI's filer id) for issuer CIK 2027882; TOTALAMOUNTSOLD $1,200,000,000. Select III Friends (CIK 2027876): $60M offered, $0 sold.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins XX
funds.note: Firm post 2022-01-11: 'KP 20, an $800m fund to back early stage companies'. Form D 0001894867-22-000001 is $800M offered, $0 sold (filed before close; no accession). KP XX Friends (CIK 1894913) Form D 0001894913-22-000001 shows $37,575,000 sold, the same figure as Select II Friends (possible co-issuer cross-wire, not listed).

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Select Fund II
funds.note: Firm post 2022-01-11: 'KP Select II, a $1 billion fund'. Form D 0001894699-22-000001 $1B offered, $0 sold (no accession). Select II Friends (CIK 1906727): $37,575,000 sold.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Select Fund (Select I)
funds.note: Firm post 2021-04-19: 'Kleiner Perkins Select, a new $750M fund'. Form D 0001853994-21-000001 $750M offered, $0 sold (no accession). The Wikipedia line 'Select I in 2021' agrees on the year.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers XIX (KP19)
funds.note: Firm post 2020-03-05: 'KP19, with $700M to focus on early-stage investments'. Form D 0001801167-20-000001 $700M offered, $0 sold (no accession). Wikipedia's '19th fund on 31 January 2019' conflates KP18 and KP19; the firm's post dates KP19 to 2020-03-05.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers XVIII (KP18)
funds.note: Crunchbase News 2019-01-31: the firm 'had raised $600 million in new capital for its 18th venture fund' (announced in a firm blog post that day; the firm's own KP19 post says 'When we announced KP18 in January of last year'). Form D 0001764543-19-000001 $600M offered, $0 sold (no accession).

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers XVII
funds.note: Crunchbase News 2019-01-31: Fund XVII (2016) was $400 million. Form D 0001678018-16-000001 (2016Q2) $400M offered, $0 sold (no accession). Wikipedia: 'In early 2016, the firm raised $1.4 billion in KP XVII and DGF III'.

funds.name: KPCB Digital Growth Fund III
funds.note: Crunchbase News 2019-01-31: '$1 billion for its third Digital Growth Fund' alongside Fund XVII in 2016. Form D 0001678000-16-000001 $1B offered, $0 sold (no accession). ADV GAV $816.5M. Managed by the growth team that left to form Bond in 2018-09; the vehicle stayed under CRD 161035 (decisions D2).

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers XVI
funds.note: Reuters 2014-06-28 (via Yahoo): filed for 'an early-stage growth fund of $450 million' KPCB XVI; Fortune 2014-04-14 gave the $450M target. Form D 0001611731-14-000001 $450M offered, $0 sold (no accession). Size is the filed offering; no separate close announcement found.

funds.name: KPCB Digital Growth Fund II
funds.note: Reuters 2014-06-28: 'a later-stage fund of $750 million'; Fortune 2014-04-14: '$750 million for its second digital growth fund, compared to its $1 billion predecessor'. Form D 0001611731-14-000002 (filed under XVI's filer prefix, issuer CIK 1611736) $750M offered, $0 sold (no accession). ADV GAV $1.04B.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers XV
funds.note: TechCrunch 2012-05-17: 'closed on a $525 million round for its fifteenth venture fund, dubbed KPCB 15'. Form D 0001547840-12-000001 $525M offered, $0 sold (no accession).

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers XIV
funds.note: Fortune 2010-10-27: KPCB XIV 'is targeting $650 million'; Fortune 2011-02-16: 'The original target was $650 million, but sources say that the final figure will be slightly higher'; TechCrunch 2012-05-17: 'The offering price for KPCB's 14th fund was $650 million'. Form D 0001505781-10-000001 $650M offered, $0 sold (no accession). Final close figure not published.

funds.name: KPCB Digital Growth Fund (I)
funds.note: Fortune 2011-02-16: 'KP recently increased the Digital Growth Fund's size to more than $1 billion' (target was $750M, Fortune 2010-10-27); TechCrunch 2012-05-17: 'In late 2010 the firm raised $1 billion for its digital growth fund'. Form D/A 0001505782-11-000001 (2011Q1): $1,000,000,000 offered, TOTALAMOUNTSOLD $932,326,251, first sale 2010-11-17. The filing does not show the full $1B, so no accession with size $1B; the alternative is size 932,326,251 with accession 0001505782-11-000001 (the build asserts size == sold).

funds.name: KPCB sFund
funds.note: TechCrunch 2010-10-21: 'a $250 million fund being led by Kleiner partner Bing Gordon'; 'Facebook, Amazon, Zynga, are major partners with Comcast, Liberty Media, and Allen & Co.' KPCB sFund, LLC Form D 0001503706-10-000001 (2010-10-21) offered only $50,000,000, $0 sold: the $250M is the announced initiative, the vehicle on file is $50M. Not on the 2026 ADV roster. Suggest describing in the basis rather than listing at $250M.

funds.name: iFund (initiative, no vehicle)
funds.note: TechCrunch 2010-03-31: 'iFund, a $100 million fund to spur iPhone app development' (2008), 'doubling ... of its iFund to $200 million'. No KPCB iFund vehicle exists on EDGAR or the ADV roster (the IFUND CIKs in entities.json are unrelated third parties, desk external); Wikipedia calls it 'a $100 million venture capital investment initiative'. An allocation from the main funds, so describe in the basis, do not list as a fund.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers XIII
funds.note: TechCrunch 2008-05-01: 'KPCB XIII, which will invest $700 million in greentech, information technology and life sciences ventures'. Paper Form D (REGDEX 2008-05-19, REGDEX/A 2009-02-02), no machine-readable amount. Conflict to flag: TechCrunch 2012-05-17 says 'its 13th fund's offering was sized at $950 million'. ADV GAV $37.2M.

funds.name: KPCB Green Growth Fund
funds.note: TechCrunch 2008-05-01: 'a standalone $500 million Green Growth Fund'. Announced size; paper Form D (REGDEX 2008-05-19, REGDEX/A 2009-02-02). ADV GAV $56.3M.

funds.name: Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers XII
funds.note: VentureBeat 2006-02-15: Kleiner 'has also finished raising its twelfth fund, at $600 million'; TechCrunch 2008-05-01: 'It raised $600 million for its twelfth fund just two years ago'. Paper Form D (REGDEX 2006-03-03 and 2009-02-02).

funds.name: KPCB Pandemic and Bio Defense Fund
funds.note: VentureBeat 2006-02-15: 'The $200 million pandemic fund, formally called the KPCB Pandemic and Bio Defense Fund'. Paper Form D (REGDEX 2006-03-03). Not on the 2026 ADV roster.

funds.name: KPCB China Fund
funds.note: SiliconANGLE 2011-11-03: 'Kleiner raised $360 million fund in its first round of investment conducted in year 2007' (decisions.md X1 also cites VentureBeat 2007-04-23, not re-read here). Paper Form D (REGDEX 2007-05-11). Reported by KPCB China Management (CRD 161470) on its own 7.B.(1), GAV $334.0M; on Kleiner Perkins' 7.B.(2). Inside the boundary only under provisional delta X1.

funds.name: KPCB China Fund II
funds.note: VentureBeat 2011-11-03: 'Kleiner Perkins has raised a $250 million fund to invest in Chinese companies, according to a filing'; SiliconANGLE same day says 'raising'. Form D 0001533831-11-000001 (2011-11-03) $250M offered, $0 sold (no accession); no close announcement found, so $250M is the filed offering. ADV 7.B.(1) of CRD 161035, GAV $445.3M. Also reported: an RMB fund 'with a target of at least $89.4 million' (SiliconANGLE), no vehicle on file. Provisional delta X1.

history_facts.fact: Founded in 1972 as Kleiner Perkins by Eugene Kleiner (a Fairchild Semiconductor founder) and Tom Perkins (an early Hewlett-Packard executive) in Menlo Park, California; renamed Kleiner, Perkins, Caufield & Byers when Frank Caufield and Brook Byers became partners (Byers joined in 1977); the first venture firm with an office on Sand Hill Road.
Genentech: co-founded in 1976 by 'a young KP partner' (the panel lists founders Herb Boyer and Bob Swanson) with the firm's seed capital.
Sun Microsystems and Compaq, both backed in 1982; Compaq is called 'one of the most important bets in KP history'.
Netscape, backed in 1994 (Wikipedia: $5 million for about 25%); its 1995 IPO priced at a $2.9 billion valuation.
Amazon, backed in 1996 (Wikipedia: returns above $1 billion on an $8 million investment).
Google, backed in 1999 at the Series A: 'We wrote our largest check ever' (Wikipedia: $12 million); John Doerr remains on Alphabet's board.
history_facts.source: https://www.kleinerperkins.com/ (panel 'Google'); https://www.kleinerperkins.com/perspectives/ post 'Parallel: Building the infrastructure for AI' 2025-11-12

history_facts.fact: The firm says it has been the earliest backer of over 1,000 companies 'including the likes of Google, Amazon and Genentech' and has returned over $35 billion to its limited partners (as of 2022-01).

Growth team (Mary Meeker) left in September 2018 to form Bond; the firm returned to early-stage investing under Mamoon Hamid (joined 2017) and Ilya Fushman (joined 2018) with the $600M KP18 in January 2019, and re-added growth with Kleiner Perkins Select ($750M) in April 2021.
Today: on 2026-03-24 the firm announced $3.5 billion: KP22, a $1 billion early-stage fund (its twenty-second), and $2.5 billion in growth funds.
Gross assets of the private funds the firm reports: $20,693,034,506 (CRD 161035, 42 funds, 2026-03-31); KPCB China Management adds $358,557,394 (CRD 161470). Sidecar only, never reader copy.

Rename: the brand changed from KPCB / Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers to Kleiner Perkins in 2018, not 2019, on the archive evidence: the last kpcb.com captures are 2018-03 and kleinerperkins.com/partnerships is captured from 2018-07-17 (sources/wayback/cc-manifest*.json). No press article dating the rename was found (two Google News queries). The legal name never changed: the 2026 ADV still reads 'Kleiner Perkins Caufield & Byers, LLC' with primary business name 'Kleiner Perkins'; fund vehicles kept the long name through XIX (2020) and dropped it from Kleiner Perkins XX (2022). decisions.md says 'until the 2019 rebrand': check before the history cites a year.

form_d_filing_style: Kleiner Perkins files a fixed total-offering amount before first close ($0 sold) and rarely amends: XIV, XV, XVI, XVII, XVIII, XIX, XX, Select I, Select II, DGF II, DGF III and China Fund II all show $0 sold, and in each case the offering equals the press or firm-stated size to the dollar (the Accel shape, exact corroboration). From 2024 the firm files at close with the full amount sold: XXI $825M, Select III $1.2B, XXII $995M, Select IV $1.92B, Flex I $555M; only those five can carry an accession. Pre-2009 funds (XII, XIII, Green Growth, Pandemic, China Fund) are paper REGDEX.
